candidates.mechanism: Dendritic target propagation: distal-dendrite top-down excitation minus learned dendrite-targeting inhibition provides a local error proxy in multilayer E/I circuits.
evidence: Five-instance setup; default supervised config train_steps=20000, epochs=1; deposited CIFAR 10-epoch job uses train_steps=40000, epochs=10.
S3/S4 optimized DTP configs use symmetric top-down B=W^T. Separate MNIST random-feedback experiment moves alignment ~45°→~60° with similar MNIST accuracy.
scope: 'Comparable to BP' is not parity: DTP trails matched EIANN-BP by 2.57–4.70 pp in recovered S3/S4 conditions.
Absolute CIFAR accuracy is low; evidence is for constrained biological credit assignment, not competitive modern vision.
Do not generalize MNIST asymmetric-feedback result to S3/S4.
No independent exact replication found.

candidates.mechanism: Offline spontaneous/noise replay plus local Hebbian plasticity suppresses cross-talk and restores latent old-task structure.
evidence: 2025 same-lab recurrent extension CIFAR-10 33.56%→81.30%, parallel reference 91.87%.
scope: Original natural-image tests use frozen/pre-extracted features.

candidates.mechanism: Nested modular recurrent topology enriches reciprocal/cyclic motifs and node-timescale diversity; cycle-preserving/destroying controls link recurrence to memory.
evidence: 100 synthetic graphs/level: higher hierarchy improves memory across α, p<0.01, CLES≥61.15%; vs degree-preserving random p<1e-33, CLES=100%.
Destroying cycles via degree-preserving rewiring reduces memory across regimes; preserving first-level modules + cycle counts recovers similar memory to level-3 hierarchy.
Multitasking higher hierarchy p<0.05, CLES≥59.18%; vs degree-random p<1e-9, CLES≥75.75%.
HCP group connectome from 327 structural networks: hierarchical null > strict modular p<1e-12, CLES≥79.5%.
Wiring-cost-normalized empirical connectome > null ensembles p<1e-30, CLES≥97.27%; simulated vs MEG timescales ρ≈0.44, p<1e-20.
scope: Fixed reservoirs + trained linear readout; not end-to-end deep learning.
Simple memory/nonlinear tasks; third hierarchy level rarely improves over second.
Cycles explain memory substantially but not all multitasking benefit.
No matched fully trainable RNN/Transformer transfer of the exact cycle-enrichment mechanism was found in this run.

candidates.mechanism: Spike-based Alignment Learning (SAL): noisy spike-timing difference distributions expose reciprocal-weight asymmetry; a synapse-local modified anti-Hebbian STDP rule adjusts feedback weights toward effective reciprocal forward weights.
evidence: Deep SymmNet benchmark uses 2 convolutional + 3 fully connected layers, five seeds, 200 epochs, alternating ANN forward-learning and SNN symmetrization phases.
Paper estimates a 320 s SAL symmetrization phase versus ~5000 s forward epoch under its cortical-timescale mapping (~6.4%); this is a modeled physical-time estimate, not measured GPU overhead.
Public plotting notebook computes each seed's mean over the final five epochs and reports mean±SD across seeds.
scope: Only fully connected feedback weights are SAL/RDD-symmetrized in the deep benchmark. For non-BP algorithms, convolutional layers use FA; BP uses exact weight transport in conv layers.
SAL remains below BP by 4.2 pp on CIFAR-10, 0.6 pp on Fashion-MNIST, and 2.0 pp on SVHN in the printed labels.
Fashion-MNIST SAL and RDD both round to 91.5%; any claimed SAL advantage there depends on unrounded means.
Public author code exists, but the inspected repository tree does not commit the raw results/symm_net/sweep files consumed by the plotting notebook.
No clear exact independent SAL reproduction/failure found.

candidates.mechanism: TD-MCL: progressively grows modular spiking subnetworks and cross-task links, then prunes connections using a feedback-guided score combining local Hebbian co-activation with global cross-task reuse/generalization.
evidence: Ablation on 10-step Split CIFAR-100: removing local Hebbian term lowers average incremental accuracy by 11.25%; removing global knowledge-generalization term lowers it by 11.77%.
Example pruning outcomes reduce retained parameter counts for tasks 1/2/3/6 to 60.66%, 60.99%, 61.09%, 77.53%; one Task-8 case reports 46.89% redundant-parameter reduction at 70% success.
First ten CIFAR-100 tasks retain 88.41% after task 10 and 88.81% after task 20 in the reported analysis.
scope: Strong AI transfer evidence for a neuro-inspired grow/reuse/prune strategy, but the exact evolutionary routing and pruning formulas are engineering mechanisms motivated by developmental neuroscience, not experimentally established biological mechanisms.
The custom developmental ordering is explicitly inspired by, not a precise infant developmental trajectory.
Independent replication not established.
Need audit of public code/data, task-ID/replay/storage assumptions, run counts, and parameter/compute accounting before stronger promotion.
